Captain Hook.objective: In order to achieve this objective, you must unlock the Hangman's Tree location by playing the Never Land Map. Peter Pan must be played, either by you or an opponent, to Hangman's Tree. You will then need to move him to Mermaid Lagoon, then to Skull Rock, and finally to the Jolly Roger, where you must defeat him to win the game.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: Place a Lock Token on Hangman's Tree, as that location is locked at the beginning of the game.

sections.title: Peter Pan
sections.text: When Peter Pan is revealed, he must immediately be played to Hangman's Tree, even if Hangman's Tree is still locked. If Peter Pan is one of the two cards drawn by an opponent while performing a Fate action targeting you, the opponent must play Peter Pan and discard the other card.

sections.title: Never Land Map
sections.text:
When you play the Never Land Map, unlock Hangman's Tree by removing the Lock Token from the location.

Important: Peter Pan may not be moved from Hangman's Tree until it is unlocked.

sections.title: Controlling Your Fate
sections.text: Unlike other Villains, Captain Hook can play and discard cards from his own Fate deck using Worthy Opponent, Give Them a Scare, and Obsession. Using these cards will help you reveal Peter Pan and bring him into your Realm as soon as possible.

sections.title: Extra Actions
sections.text:
Cannon, Hook's Case, and Ingenious Device are Items that add extra action symbols to your Realm. After the Item has been played to a location, you may perform the extra action in addition to the other available actions there.

Example: If Cannon has been played to Skull Rock, you may perform five actions when you are at Skull Rock: its four action symbols plus the Vanquish action from Cannon.

sections.title: Curses
sections.text:
Curse is a card type unique to Maleficent. Curses are played to locations, and each one has an Ability that affects Heroes at that location. However, each Curse also has an action that will cause it to be discarded, so you'll need to strategize when and where to play each Curse.

Multiple Curses may be played to the same location, and a Curse may be moved using a Move an Item or Ally action.

The three Curses are Forest of Thorns, Green Fire, and Dreamless Sleep.

sections.title: Forest of Thorns
sections.text:
Forest of Thorns makes it difficult for opponents to play a Hero at its location because a Hero must have a Strength of 4 or more to be played there.

Beware: If a qualifying Hero is played to its location, Forest of Thorns is discarded.

sections.title: Green Fire
sections.text:
Green Fire is a very powerful Curse because Heroes cannot be played to its location.

Beware: If Maleficent ever moves to its location, Green Fire is discarded.

sections.title: Dreamless Sleep
sections.text:
Dreamless Sleep reduces the Strengths of all Heroes at its location by 2.

Beware: If you play an Ally to its location, Dreamless Sleep is discarded.

Note: You may move an Ally to a location with Dreamless Sleep without having to discard the Curse. Also, you can play Dreamless Sleep to a location that already has Allies without affecting the Allies or the Curse.

sections.title: Other Cards
sections.text:
Vanish allows Maleficent to remain at a location, enabling her to take the same actions two turns in a row.

Raven is a powerful Ally to play as early as possible. At the start of each turn, you may move Raven and perform one action that is available at his new location.

Note: Raven may not take Fate actions.

Prince John.objective:
Prince John is all about greed, so he needs to accumulate Power. However, as tempting as it might be to save all the Power you can, you will need to spend some Power in order to win.

Several Heroes can hinder Prince John's ability to gain Power. It is a good idea to play Allies, even before any Heroes have been played. By doing so, you will be prepared to Vanquish a Hero that is affecting your progress.

sections.title: The Jail
sections.text:
Prince John's Realm has a location that can be used to his advantage. The Jail does not have any action symbols that can be covered by Heroes, making Heroes at that location less disruptive. Prince John has Imprison cards which allow him to move Heroes to The Jail in order to make actions available elsewhere.

Note: When at The Jail, Heroes' Abilities are still in effect.

sections.title: It's Good to Be the King!
sections.text: Although Heroes can be disruptive to his plans, Prince John has several tricks up his sleeve. Cards such as Warrant, Sheriff of Nottingham, and Beautiful, Lovely Taxes allow him to profit from having Heroes in his Realm. Sometimes it pays to keep your enemies close!

sections.title: Special Fate Cards
sections.text:
When Steal from the Rich is played, 4 Power is taken from Prince John and placed on any one Hero that is in his Realm. When a Hero that has Power on them is defeated, Prince John takes all of the Power back.

The same Hero may be used to Steal from the Rich multiple times, which can lead to a big payoff when the Hero is defeated!

sections.title: Robin Hood
sections.text: While Robin Hood is in Prince John's Realm, every time Prince John gains Power due to an action or card, he gains 1 less Power than he would normally gain. It is usually a good idea to defeat Robin Hood as soon as possible!

sections.title: Little John
sections.text: When Little John is played, 4 Power is taken from Prince John and placed on Little John's card. When Little John is defeated, Prince John takes all of the Power back. Waiting for just the right time to defeat Little John can help set up an unexpected victory!

Jafar.objective:
To achieve Jafar's Objective, you must unlock the Cave of Wonders with the Scarab Pendant. Then the Magic Lamp must be played to the Cave of Wonders, which also brings Genie to the same location. You must Hypnotize Genie, which puts Genie under Jafar's control, and move the Magic Lamp to Sultan's Palace.

Important: To win, the Magic Lamp must be on your side of the Board.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: Place a Lock Token on the Cave of Wonders, as that location is locked at the beginning of the game.

sections.title: Scarab Pendant
sections.text: Playing the Scarab Pendant is the first step to achieving victory. When you play the Scarab Pendant, unlock the Cave of Wonders by removing the Lock Token from the location. Additionally, while the Scarab Pendant is in your Realm, you may draw an extra card at the end of each turn.

sections.title: Magic Lamp
sections.text:
After the Cave of Wonders has been unlocked, you may play the Magic Lamp to that location. When you play the Magic Lamp, immediately find Genie and play him to the Cave of Wonders.

Note: If Genie is under Jafar's control when the Magic Lamp is played, he is no longer under Jafar's control.

sections.title: Get What You Need
sections.text: You will want to play the Scarab Pendant and the Magic Lamp as soon as possible. Scrying and Gazeem are cards that can help you find them.

sections.title: Under Your Control
sections.text: Jafar is able to Hypnotize Heroes. When you Hypnotize a Hero, you defeat them and move them to the bottom of your Board. The Hypnotized Hero is now under your control and is treated as an Ally with the same Strength. When a Hypnotized Hero is used to defeat another Hero, they are both discarded to the Fate discard pile.

sections.title: Activated Abilities
sections.text:
Jafar has some cards with Activated Abilities. See the Instructions for details on how cards with Activated Abilities are played and their Abilities activated.

Iago may be used to move the Magic Lamp toward Sultan's Palace. Snake Staff can help you get a Hypnotize card when you are ready to put Genie under your control. Giant Hourglass weakens Heroes to make them easier to Hypnotize or defeat.

sections.title: Activated Abilities
sections.text: Queen of Hearts has some cards with Activated Abilities, such as Card Guard and Stopwatch. See the Instructions for details on how cards with Activated Abilities are played and their Abilities activated.

sections.title: Card Guards / Wickets
sections.text:
Card Guards are played like other Allies, and may be used to defeat Heroes. However, if you activate a Card Guard's Activated Ability, it is converted into a Wicket and is no longer considered a Card Guard. Rotate the card 90 degrees to indicate that it is a Wicket.

Wickets may not be used to defeat Heroes. However, you may convert a Wicket back to a Card Guard by activating its Ability again.

Note: A Wicket is still considered to be an Ally. Their Strength is affected by any Abilities on cards that are in your Realm. In addition, Spears may be added to Wickets to increase their Strength, thereby increasing your chances of successfully taking a shot.

sections.title: Take the Shot
sections.text: If there is at least one Wicket at each location in your Realm, you may play Take the Shot to attempt to win the game. Reveal the top five cards of your Villain deck and add up the total Cost of those cards. If the total Cost of the revealed cards is lower than the total Strength of all of the Wickets in your Realm, then you make the shot and win the game! If you do not make the shot, discard the five revealed cards and try again later.

sections.title: Shrinking Heroes
sections.text:
Makes You Smaller and Fury allow Queen of Hearts to Shrink Heroes. When a Hero is Shrunk, rotate the Hero 45 degrees so that only one action symbol is covered by the corner of the card, leaving the other action available.

If there are multiple Heroes at a location with a Shrunken Hero, the Shrunken Hero is the only Hero that covers up an action symbol. The other Heroes do not cover any actions until the Shrunken Hero is moved or defeated.

sections.title: Enlarging Heroes
sections.text: When an opponent plays Makes You Larger, they choose a Hero in your Realm and Enlarge it. The Hero card is rotated 90 degrees so that it covers one action symbol at an adjacent location in addition to the two action symbols at the Hero's location. Your opponent chooses which action to cover.

Ursula.objective: Important: To win, the Trident and the Crown must be on your side of the Board.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: Place a Lock Token on The Palace, as that location is locked at the beginning of the game.

sections.title: Changing Form
sections.text:
Ursula's Realm has a locked location, but it functions differently than in other Villains' Realms. The Lock Token is never removed from Ursula's Realm.

Each time you play Change Form, the Lock Token is moved between The Palace and Ursula's Lair, unlocking one location and locking the other.

Both locations have useful actions, so choosing when to play Change Form is very important.

sections.title: The Trident
sections.text:
When you play the Trident, immediately find King Triton and play him to the same location. Then move the Trident to the other side of the Board and attach it to King Triton.

When King Triton is defeated, the Trident is returned to your side of the Board at the location King Triton was defeated.

sections.title: Binding Contracts
sections.text:
Ursula is unique in that she does not have a Vanquish action in her Realm. Instead, Ursula defeats Heroes by using Binding Contracts. When you play a Binding Contract, attach it to a Hero. (Binding Contracts are one of the rare instances where an Item from the Villain deck can be attached to a Hero.)

Each Binding Contract is tied to a location in Ursula's Realm. A Hero with a Binding Contract attached to them is defeated when they are moved to the location specified on the card. Discard the Hero to your Fate discard pile and discard the Binding Contract to your Villain discard pile.

Example: A Hero with the Binding Contract for The Shore attached is defeated when you move them to The Shore.

Captain Hook [I2E].objective:
The Villainous Captain Hook's only goal in life is to defeat pesky Peter Pan, but it's not a simple task! Peter Pan is a tricky foe and has the Lost Boys and Tinker Bell to protect him. He's even recruited Heroes like Wendy and her brothers from London.

As Captain Hook, you must lure Peter Pan into the Lost Boys Hideout. Then, you need to get him to your ship, the Jolly Roger, where you will surely have the edge. With the help of your Allies, especially Smee and Mr. Starkey, try to defeat Peter Pan before any of the other villains complete their objective and prove that you are the greatest Pirate Captain of them all!

sections.title: First, Find Peter Pan
sections.text: Peter Pan is hiding in your Fate deck. He might appear when your opponents Fate you, but you can also reveal cards from your Fate deck by playing Worthy Opponent, Obsession, or Neverland Map.

sections.title: Then, Move Peter Pan to Jolly Roger
sections.text:
When Peter Pan is played, he's played to the Lost Boys Hideout. You'll have to move him one location at a time to the Jolly Roger with the Move Hero action on your board.

Playing Ingenious Device allows you to add the Move Hero action to any location.

sections.title: Finally, Defeat Peter Pan
sections.text:
Use your Allies to defeat Peter Pan (and other Heroes) with the Vanquish action.

Play Cannon to add a Vanquish action to any location.

Maleficent [I2E].objective:
Maleficent wasn't invited to the christenin of Princess Aurora, and now she wants to take her revenge by cursing the entire kingdom.

Spread your Allies - like the goons and the Raven - throughout the Realm so that you can play Curses to locations with an Ally. But you must be wary of the Heroes! The good fairies - Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather - as well as Prince Philip and Aurora will do their best to foil your plans.

If you can play a Curse at every location in the Realm before any other villain achieves their goal, then you'll prove that you're the Mistress of All Evil!

sections.title: Curses!
sections.text:
Curses are unique to Maleficent's deck and each type has a unique benefit when it's in your Realm. However, cards in your Fate deck and other actions will cause the Curses to be discarded. You may play a Curse to any location, as long as there's an Ally at the location. You cannot play Curses to Ravens current location. Multiple Curses may be played to the same location, and, once played, you may move Curses using the Move an Item or Ally action.

To find the Curses or Allies in your deck, you can move to a location with the Discard action and discard multiple cards from your hand to help you cycle through your cards. Playing cards like Tyranny will also help!

sections.title: Be Ready for the Heroes
sections.text: The Heroes in your Fate deck will slow you down. Play Allies to the bottom of your Realm to play Curses and to defeat Heroes with the Vanquish action. Malice and Dragon Form also help you defeat Heroes.

Prince John [I2E].objective:
While King Richard is away, the Villainous Prince John wants to grab all the money and Power. Unfortunately, P.J. is constantly plagued by the do-gooder Robin Hood and his band of Heroes. Prince John's plan is to put Robin Hood in jail, take all the power, and show that he is the greatest villain ever.

As Prince John, you must balance hoarding Power to reach your goal and spending it on Ally and Effect cards to draw Robin Hood into Sherwood Forest and defeat him. Do it all before the other villains complete their objectives to be the winner!

sections.title: Gain Power
sections.text: There are several ways for Prince John to gain Power. First, you can move to a location on your board with a Gain Power action to gain 1, 2, or 3 Power. You can also gain Power from Heroes in your Realm with Warrant, Sheriff of Nottingham, and Beautiful, Lovely Taxes and from other players with Greed.

sections.title: Be Ready to Vanquish Heroes
sections.text: In your Fate deck, Steal from the Rich will take Power from you and give it to the Heroes. But you can gain it back when you defeat those Heroes, so you'll want to have Allies played and ready to Vanquish when you need to! Little John actually reduces the Power Prince John can gain each turn so you'll want to Vanquish him as well.

sections.title: Find Robin Hood and Defeat Him!
sections.text: Robin Hood may turn up when an opponent Fates you, but if he doesn't, you can play Set a Trap and Cowardice to find him or defeat Maid Marian. When you defeat Robin Hood, he's automatically thrown in The Jail.

Ursula [I2E].objective:
Ursula, the Villainous Sea Witch, wants to rule the ocean. But first, she'll need to use her magic powers to claim the Crown and Trident - two of Triton's most prized possessions.

The Heroes, led by Ariel, Triton, and Eric, will do their best to stop her. Ursula will need to play Binding Contracts to Vanquish the Heroes with 'her babies', Flotsam and Jetsam, who never leave her side once played. If she can get Triton's Items to her Lair before the other villains complete their objectives, she'll prove that she's the true Queen of the Ocean and greatest villain of them all!

sections.title: First, Find the Trident and Crown
sections.text: There are several cards in your deck that will help you find other cards, including Whirlpool, Divination, and Opportunist. Moving to the location with the Discard action and discarding multiple cards from your hand will also help you cycle through your cards!

sections.title: Then, Move the Items to Ursula's Lair
sections.text: Once you've found and played the Trident and the Crown, use the Move Item action to move them to Ursula's Lair.

sections.title: Keep Heroes Out of Your Way!
sections.text: Several of the Heroes in your Fate deck will try to mess with your plan by moving Items and blocking actions. Normally, Heroes are defeated with Allies using the Vanquish action. Ursula doesn't have any Vanquish actions on her board. She will need to play Binding Contracts to locations to gain one-time-use Vanquish actions.

Evil Queen.objective: In order to achieve Evil Queen's Objective, you must unlock the Dwarfs' Cottage by playing four different Ingredients. You will also need to Brew Poison, which is used to defeat Heroes in your Realm, including Snow White. Snow White must be played, either by you or an opponent. Finally, you will need to play Take a Bite when you are at Snow White's location in order to defeat her and win the game.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: Place a Lock Token on the Dwarfs' Cottage, as that location is locked at the beginning of the game.

sections.title: Ingredients
sections.text:
Ingredient is a card type unique to Evil Queen. Ingredients function the same as Effects, with one exception. The first time you play each Ingredient, after doing what it says, put it below your Board. If you play an Ingredient that youve played before, do what it says, then discard it.

As soon as you have played each of the four Ingredients (Scream of Fright, Old Hag's Cackle, Mummy Dust, and Black of Night), unlock the Dwarfs' Cottage by removing the Lock Token from the location. The four Ingredients remain below your Board for the rest of the game.

sections.title: Activated Abilities
sections.text: Evil Queen has some cards with Activated Abilities. See the Instructions for details on how cards with Activated Abilities are played and their Abilities activated.

sections.title: Magic Mirror
sections.text:
Evil Queen can use her Magic Mirror to find Snow White. To activate this Ability, perform an Activate action and pay 3 Power. Then find Snow White and play her to the Dwarfs' Cottage, even if it is locked.

In addition, while the Magic Mirror is in your Realm, each time you are the target of a Fate action, you may draw a card.

sections.title: Poison Apples
sections.text: Evil Queen does not have a Vanquish action in her Realm. Instead, she uses poison apples to defeat Heroes. To do this, she must Brew Poison and then get a Hero to Take A Bite.

sections.title: Brew Poison Action
sections.text:
The Brew Poison action is unique to Evil Queen and is found at the Laboratory location. Each time you perform this action, you may convert as many of your Power as you wish into Poison. Move the Power onto your Board to indicate that it is now Poison.

Note: Poison is no longer considered Power. Poison may not be used to pay a card or Ability's Cost. Having Poison or adding Power from the Supply to your Poison do not trigger Conditions that require having Power or gaining Power.

sections.title: Take A Bite
sections.text:
When you play Take A Bite, Evil Queen must be at the same location as the Hero being defeated. You must also pay Poison equal to the Hero's Strength, which may be modified by other cards in the Realm. Remove that many Poison from your Board and return it to the Supply. Discard the defeated Hero to your Fate discard pile, and discard Take A Bite to your Villain discard pile.

Note: If you do not have enough Poison to defeat a Hero, you may not play Take a Bite.

Dr. Facilier.objective:
Dr. Facilier is unique because during the game, you and your opponents will put cards into a Fortune pile. When you play The Cards Will Tell, cards will be revealed from the Fortune pile, and you will receive the rewards or consequences of those cards.

To achieve Dr. Facilier's Objective, you must reveal the card Rule New Orleans from the Fortune pile. However, you also must control the Talisman.

Important: To win, the Talisman must be on your side of the Board.

sections.title: Fortune Pile
sections.text:
Dr. Facilier has a Fortune pile that is separate from his decks and discard piles. You need to play Rule New Orleans in order to put it into the Fortune pile before you can win. You can also play Friends on the Other Side to add it to the pile and gain Power. However, you want to keep your Fortune pile small, to give yourself a better chance of ruling New Orleans. Your opponents will be adding other, less helpful cards to the Fortune pile. Use Desperation and Illusion Powder to remove cards from the Fortune pile.

Keep the Fortune pile face up below your Board. The cards in the Fortune pile are public information.

Note: Cards are only put into or removed from the Fortune pile if a card Ability specifically instructs you to do so.

sections.title: Fortune Abilities
sections.text:
Some cards in Dr. Facilier's deck have Fortune Abilities. These Abilities are ignored when the cards are played, and are only resolved when revealed from the Fortune pile by playing The Cards Will Tell.

Note: Cards without Fortune Abilities may still be put into the Fortune pile. When revealed, they are discarded without any effect.

sections.title: The Cards Will Tell
sections.text:
When you play The Cards Will Tell, shuffle the cards in the Fortune pile face down, fan them out, and have an opponent reveal three at random. Resolve all Fortune Abilities on the revealed cards, in the order of your choice.

Note: You may still play The Cards Will Tell if there are fewer than three cards in the Fortune pile. Reveal and resolve them all.

sections.title: Pay Back Your Debt
sections.text:
All the spirits are Allies, and may be moved and used to defeat Heroes as normal. However, when an opponent adds cards to the Fortune pile, they may convince the spirits to turn against you and collect on your debt.

When Shadow Spirits are revealed from the Fortune pile, they force you to lose two Power.

When Masked Spirits are revealed from the Fortune pile, they stop you from resolving the Fortune Abilities of other cards, including Shadow Spirits and Rule New Orleans. All Masked Spirits that were revealed are discarded, even if there's more than one, and all other revealed cards are returned to the Fortune pile without being resolved. In addition, Masked Spirits are unique because they are considered both an Ally and an Item.

sections.title: Control the Talisman
sections.text:
To win the game, you must have the Talisman under your control when Rule New Orleans' Fortune Ability is resolved. It can be difficult to keep control of the Talisman, so you'll need to strategize the best time to play it.

If you have the Talisman when a Hero with a Strength of 3 or less is played, that Hero steals it from you. Move the Talisman to the top of the Board and attach it to the Hero. When that Hero is defeated, the Talisman is returned to your side of the Board at the location the Hero was defeated.

Note: If a Hero already has the Talisman when a new Hero is played, the Talisman does not move. It remains with the Hero it is attached to.

Hades.objective:
To achieve Hades' Objective, you must play Titans to The Underworld and move them across your Realm to Mount Olympus.

Important: Trapped Titans do not count toward your Objective. However, you can win even if there are additional Titans trapped in your Realm.

sections.title: Titans
sections.text:
Titan is a card type unique to Hades. You must lead at least three Titans to Mount Olympus in order to achieve victory. There are five Titans in your deck and each one has a powerful Ability.

Titans function much like your Allies, but they must be played to The Underworld. You may move a Titan using the Move an Item or Ally action. Don't forget to use the Titan's Ability each time he is moved.

Just like Allies, Titans may be used to defeat Heroes by performing the Vanquish action. However, because they are still discarded when used to defeat a Hero, this could set you back in getting Titans to Mount Olympus.

sections.title: Trapped
sections.text:
During the game, Titans may be trapped by cards in your Fate deck. Rotate the card 90 degrees to indicate that the Titan is trapped.

While a Titan is trapped, their Ability is ignored. They may not be moved or used to defeat a Hero. In addition, trapped Titans do not count toward your Objective.

You can untrap Titans by playing Planets Align, or by using Pyros' Ability. When you untrap a Titan, rotate the card back to its normal position to indicate that it is no longer trapped.

sections.title: Make Them Mortal
sections.text: Mortality Potion will help you defeat Heroes without sacrificing your Titans. If you play Mortality Potion on a Hero, you'll be able to use Titans to defeat that Hero without discarding the Titans. Any Allies used are discarded as normal.

sections.title: Ride Your Chariot
sections.text: Chariot will give you extra actions during the game. After performing your normal actions, if Chariot is at your location, you may 'ride' the Chariot to any other location and perform one available action there. Chariot may only be used once per turn and may not be used to perform a Fate action. You may use Chariot in the same turn you play it.

sections.title: Let's Get Ready to Rumble
sections.text:
In addition to the Move an Item or Ally action, you can use Get Ready to Rumble! to move Titans toward Mount Olympus. You may either pay 2 Power to move a Titan one location or pay 5 Power to move a Titan two locations. You may only move one Titan when you play this card, and you may not move trapped Titans.

Note: If you move a Titan two locations, it is considered a single move and the Titan effectively jumps over the first location. Only Abilities at the Titan's final location are triggered by the move. Any Abilities at the jumped location are not triggered.

Ratigan.objective: Important: Ratigan's Objective can change. If The Robot Queen is discarded from your Realm, your new Objective is to defeat Basil.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: Place Ratigan's Objective Tile on the left side of the Board so The Superior Mind is showing.

sections.title: The Robot Queen
sections.text:
To achieve Ratigans Objective, you must find The Robot Queen, play it to The Secret Lair, and move it to Buckingham Palace. Plan ahead so you can pay The Robot Queen's Cost, which is normally 15 Power.

Some cards help you find The Robot Queen. If you play Fidget's List, you can later activate it to draw the next Item from your deck. Playing Greatest Criminal Mind lets you either gain Power or draw extra cards.

Other cards help you reduce the Cost to play The Robot Queen. The card Tools is good to play as early as possible, as it reduces the Cost of all Items. The card Gears also reduces the Cost of an Item, but it is discarded when it is used.

sections.title: Marvelous Trap
sections.text:
Marvelous Trap is a powerful card that can defeat all Heroes at its location, but it must first be set up and takes time to deploy.

First play the trap to any location. Then, when you perform the Activate action, you can pay 1 Power to activate it. Leave the Power on the card to indicate that its been activated and will go off at the start of your next turn.

If there are no Heroes at the trap's location when it goes off, it is still discarded. If the trap is discarded before it goes off, no Heroes are defeated. When Marvelous Trap is discarded, return the Power on it to the supply.

Note: If you have The Robot Queen at Buckingham Palace and The Mouse Queen is defeated with a trap, you do not immediately win. You must wait until the start of your next turn to see if you still achieve your Objective.

sections.title: The Great Mouse Detective
sections.text:
Basil is Ratigans most formidable adversary. When Basil is played or moved, he discards an Item from his new location. Some Fate cards can move Basil, making him a constant threat to your Items, including The Robot Queen.

If Basil discards The Robot Queen, flip the Objective Tile so The Rat is showing. Your new Objective is to defeat Basil.

Note: Once Ratigan's Objective changes, it cannot change back. You must defeat Basil to win.

sections.title: The Secret Lair
sections.text:
Ratigan has a location that can be used to his advantage. The Secret Lair does not have any action symbols at the top, making Heroes at that location less disruptive. Ratigan has Capture cards which allow him to move Heroes to The Secret Lair.

If you capture the Hero Flaversham, you'll reduce the Cost to play The Robot Queen. Your Ally Fidget will help you find and play Flaversham so you can later capture him.

Note: When at The Secret Lair, Heroes' Abilities are still in effect.

Scar.objective:
Scar is unique because during the game, you will put Heroes you defeat into a Succession pile instead of the Fate discard pile. If the Heroes in your Succession pile have a total Strength of 15 or more at the start of your turn, you achieve your Objective. However, you cannot start putting Heroes in your Succession pile until you defeat Mufasa.

Note: You may defeat other Heroes before defeating Mufasa. However, they are discarded to your Fate discard pile instead of being put into the Succession pile.

sections.title: Controlling Your Fate
sections.text:
Your first step toward your Objective is to find and defeat Mufasa, who is in your Fate deck.

Long Live The King lets you reveal four cards from your Fate deck, which will help you quickly find and play Mufasa.

Whisper allows you to play any card from your Fate discard pile, in case Mufasa is discarded by an opponent. You can also use Whisper to play Hakuna Matata in order to move a Hero in your Realm to any location.

After you defeat Mufasa, both Long Live The King and Whisper will help you play Heroes so you can quickly defeat them and add them to the Succession pile.

sections.title: Succession Pile
sections.text:
Scar has a Succession pile that is separate from his decks and discard piles. When you defeat Mufasa, put him into the Succession pile instead of in the Fate discard pile. For the rest of the game, all Heroes you defeat are put into the Succession pile. Keep the Succession pile face up below your Board. The cards in the Succession pile are public information.

Items are not put into the Succession pile. If a Hero has a Prophecy attached to them when they are defeated, the Prophecy is discarded to the Fate discard pile.

Important: The Succession pile is not considered to be in your Realm. The Abilities of Heroes in the Succession pile are ignored, and no cards can be played directly to the Succession pile.

sections.title: Hyenas
sections.text:
Hyenas are the Allies that you'll most often use to defeat Heroes, and the more Hyenas there are, the stronger they become. Hungry Hyenas get additional Strength for each other Hyena at their location.

Simba is a Hero that limits the Strength of all Hyenas in your Realm. If a Hyena would have a Strength of more than 2, their Strength is reduced to 2 until Simba is defeated.

Example: There are three Hyenas at Pride Rock, including Ed. Normally each Hungry Hyena's Strength would be 3 and Ed's would be 2. However, Simba limits each Hyenas Strength to 2. If you perform a Vanquish action to defeat Simba, whose Strength is 5, you must discard all three Allies.

sections.title: Leaders of the Pack
sections.text:
The Hyenas Shenzi, Banzai, and Ed are Allies that help you gain or save Power. By playing them as early as possible, you can use their Abilities to play more Hyenas, which you'll use to defeat Heroes.

Shenzi lets you play another Hyena for free.

Banzai gains you Power when other Hyenas at his location are discarded, even if Banzai is discarded in the same action. For example, if you perform a Vanquish action using Banzai and two Hungry Hyenas, you gain 2 Power.

Ed reduces the Cost to play Hyenas to his location.

Note: Shenzi, Banzai, and Ed are Hyenas. Any card that refers to Hyenas includes them.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: Instead of having a single Fate deck, Yzma has four. Shuffle your Fate cards and deal them evenly to form four Fate decks-one at each location. Place them above your Board, leaving space for Heroes.

sections.title: Finding Kuzco
sections.text:
To achieve Yzma's Objective, you'll need to find Kuzco, who is in one of your Fate decks.

Eavesdrop lets you look at all the cards in one Fate deck, which is the safest way to search for Kuzco.

After Them! reveals the cards in a Fate deck and plays all the Heroes to that location. This is most useful if you know which Fate deck Kuzco is in. But be careful-if you ever reveal Wrong Lever, you lose Power.

Smash It With A Hammer reveals and discards two cards from a Fate deck, allowing you to get rid of troublesome Fate cards like On The Run and Beware The Groove. But if you discard Kuzco, he gets reshuffled into your Fate decks.

sections.title: Controlling Kronk
sections.text:
Kronk is a powerful Ally and essential to your Objective, but he can turn against you. Each time Kronk is moved, whether by an action or card Ability, put 1 Power from the Supply on him. When he has 3 or more Power on him, he becomes a Hero. Put him at the top of your Board at the same location. He has the same Strength, but ignore his Ability-moving him when hes a Hero does not add Power.

The Path That Rocks lets you gain the Power on Kronk, whether hes an Ally or a Hero. Right-Hand Man can be used to put Kronk into your hand, whether he is close to turning, already a Hero, or still in your deck.

Note: Removing Power from Kronk when hes a Hero does not turn him back into an Ally.

sections.title: Yzma's Fate
sections.text:
When an opponent targets you with a Fate action, they must choose one of your Fate decks, secretly look at all the cards in it, and choose one card to play. If they choose to play a Hero, that Hero must be played to the location of the Fate deck it came from. All other cards are shuffled and returned to that Fate deck. If none of the cards can be played, all of them are returned.

Note: Since your opponents do not reveal the cards, they can choose not to play Wrong Lever, unless there are no other cards they can play.

If a Fate deck is empty, do not shuffle the discard pile yet-your opponents will choose from only the remaining Fate decks. However, if all of the Fate decks are empty, shuffle the discard pile and deal the cards as evenly as possible to form four new Fate decks.

Example: An opponent targets you with a Fate action. They choose the Fate deck at The Palace and look at all the cards in that deck. They choose to play Bucky, who must be played to the same location.

Note: There is no limit to the number of Heroes at a location. Move the Fate deck to make room, and offset the Heroes so all cards can be seen.

Pete.objective: To achieve Petes Objective, you must complete each of the four Goals in your Realm. You may complete them in any order. When you complete a Goal, reveal that Goal Token and then remove it from your Board.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text:
Turn the five Goal Tokens face down, mix them up, and place one at each location. Set the remaining Goal Token aside. You may look at the Goal Tokens at any time, but keep them secret from the other players.

Note: Once a Goal Token has been revealed, it can never be turned face down again.

sections.title: Goal: Power Play
sections.text:
Spend at least 6 Power in one turn while Pete is at this location.

Being able to play more than one card at the same location will make this Goal easier. If this Goal is at a location with multiple Play a Card actions, you have more options to play cards. However, if only one Play a Card action is available, you can use Bandit's ability to play at least three Bandits with one action.

sections.title: Goal: Rule the Realm
sections.text:
Start your turn with more Allies than Heroes at each location.

This Goal is completed by playing multiple Allies. Cricket can help secure this Goal by moving to any location when a Hero is played to it.

sections.title: Goal: Win Big
sections.text:
Gain at least 4 Power from playing Play a Game at this location.

Complete this Goal when you play Play A Game and reveal cards with a total Cost of at least 4 Power.

You can improve your chance by using Mischief or Sneaky Pete to put cards with a high Cost on top of your deck.

sections.title: Strike It Rich
sections.text:
Start your turn with at least three Items at this location.

Pete's deck contains four Items that can only be played to their specified location. Pete does not need to be at that location to play them.

You may complete this Goal on the start of your next turn after moving at least three Items to the Goal's location. Horse and Steamboat Willie can help you achieve this goal by quickly moving Items to the Goal's location.

sections.title: Goal: Round Up
sections.text:
Start your turn with Allies totaling at least 10 Strength at this location.

Playing many Allies with high Strength to this Goal's location is the easiest way to complete it. Bandit and Horse help you play and move Allies to the Goal's location.

sections.title: Extra Actions
sections.text: Each of Pete's Items adds an extra action symbol to your Realm. After the Item has been played to a location, you may perform the extra action in addition to the other available actions there.

Cruella de Vil.objective: To achieve Cruella De Vil's Objective, you must add Puppy Tokens from the Supply to locations in your Realm, then capture them.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: Turn the 12 Puppy Tokens face down (red side showing), mix them up, and keep them in a pile next to your Board to form a Supply.

sections.title: Puppy Tokens
sections.text:
Puppy Tokens represent the puppies that Cruella De Vil must capture, with each Puppy Token representing either 11 or 22 puppies.

In order to capture Puppy Tokens, they must first be taken from the Supply and added to your Realm. Each Puppy Token features one of the four locations in your Realm. When adding a Puppy Token to your Realm, reveal the Puppy Token and place it face up at the location specified.

Note: Each time you add a Puppy Token to your Realm, you may choose one from the Supply that is face up or face down. Once a Puppy Token has been revealed, it can never be turned face down again, even if it is returned to the Supply.

Note: Place captured Puppy Tokens below your Board, keeping them face up so all players can see how many puppies have been captured.

sections.title: Activated Abilities
sections.text:
Cruella De Vil has some cards with Activated Abilities. See the Instructions for details on how cards with Activated Abilities are played and their Abilities activated.

Flashlight and Horace bring Puppy Tokens into your Realm. Horace and Jasper capture Puppy Tokens from your Realm. Telephone can help put Horace and Jasper back into play from your discard pile.

sections.title: Roadster
sections.text: Roadster can help you move Puppy Tokens to locations so they can be more easily captured. When moved, Roadster can move to any location.

sections.title: Horace and Jasper
sections.text:
Cruella DeVil has only two Allies, and they must be used to capture puppies and defeat Heroes. Getting them into your Realm quickly and keeping them there will be important to obtaining your Objective.

You Idiots! allows you to choose an Ally from your deck and put them into your hand. This will help get Horace or Jasper into play quickly.

When an Ally with Fireplace Poker attached to them is used to defeat a Hero, you may discard Fireplace Poker instead of that Ally, allowing them to stay in your Realm longer.

If Telephone is in your Realm, it can be activated to choose an Ally from your discard pile and play it to any location.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: Place the Rapunzel Tile at Rapunzel's Tower.

sections.title: Trust
sections.text:
Mother Gothel wants to keep Rapunzel close, so she needs Rapunzel to trust her. If a card instructs you to gain Trust, take Power from the Supply equal to that amount and place it onto your Board to indicate that it is now Trust.

Note: Trust is no longer considered Power. Trust may not be used to pay a card or Ability's Cost. Having Trust or adding Power from the Supply to your Trust do not trigger Conditions that require having Power or gaining Power.

sections.title: Rapunzel
sections.text:
Rapunzel is a unique Hero because she is already in your Realm at the start of the game, and she is never discarded. Like other Heroes, she blocks actions at her location and may be defeated by using a Vanquish action.

However, when Rapunzel is defeated, instead of discarding her, move her to Rapunzel's Tower.

Important: At the end of Mother Gothel's turn, move Rapunzel one location toward Corona. If you cannot move Rapunzel because she is already at Corona, Mother Gothel loses 1 Trust.

sections.title: Controlling Rapunzel
sections.text:
Mother Gothel is able to gain Trust easily when Rapunzel is at Rapunzel's Tower, and keeping her away from Corona is important. Mother Gothel has several ways she controls Rapunzel's location.

Mother Knows Best prevents Rapunzel from moving toward Corona at the end of that turn.

Patchy Stabbington and Sideburns Stabbington move Rapunzel to Rapunzel's Tower and are powerful Allies that can be used to defeat Heroes.

Now I'm The Bad Guy moves Rapunzel to Rapunzel's Tower. Mother Gothel loses 1 Trust, but it might be helpful in combination with other actions.

sections.title: Gaining Trust
sections.text:
There are several cards that can gain Trust.

When Hair Brush is played or moved to Rapunzel's location, gain 1 Trust. This Item is good to play early as it can keep gaining Trust when it is in your Realm.

I Love You Most gains 1 Trust if Mother Gothel is at Rapunzel's location. It is most effective when played at Rapunzel's Tower to gain an additional Trust.

Let Down Your Hair can gain you Trust or move Rapunzel to help keep her away from Corona.

Misdirection gains 1 Trust but moves Rapunzel toward Corona, so it should be used strategically to avoid losing Trust later.

Crown can be used as a way to gain Power each time a Hero is defeated at that location. You can instead choose to discard Crown to gain 1 Trust.

Revenge allows you to perform a Vanquish action and gain 1 Trust if a Hero other than Rapunzel is defeated.

sections.title: Strategy Tips
sections.text:
Some cards are most effective if played when Rapunzel is at Rapunzel's Tower. Since Rapunzel will move toward Corona at the end of your turn, moving her to Rapunzel's Tower or keeping her there will allow you to gain more Trust from those cards.

Playing Effect or Condition cards and using Allies to defeat Rapunzel can move her to Rapunzel's Tower.

Horned King.objective: As the Horned King, your goal is to control the world using your Cauldron Born warriors. To do so, you must first claim The Black Cauldron. Once it is in your possession, you must power The Black Cauldron. Finally, you must use The Black Cauldron’s Ability to swap your Ancient Soldiers for Cauldron Born. Once you have Cauldron Born in all four locations, you control the world and win the game!

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: The Black Cauldron tile is a Relic, a card type unique to the Horned King. Set The Black Cauldron tile to the side of your Realm. Once you claim it, set it above your portrait on your player board with The Black Cauldron side showing.

sections.title: Claiming The Black Cauldron
sections.text:
You must have The Black Cauldron to win. You cannot lose The Black Cauldron once you claim it. Show Me The Black Cauldron allows you to claim The Black Cauldron immediately.

We Have Made a Bargain allows you to remove Dyrnwyn from your Realm and exchange it for The Black Cauldron.

We Got You Now, Pig Keeper allows you to find and place Hen Wen. Vanquishing Hen Wen allows you to claim The Black Cauldron.

These three cards have additional powers besides gaining The Black Cauldron. So, plan ahead and use them as you think best.

sections.title: Powering The Black Cauldron
sections.text:
You may power The Black Cauldron either by playing Our Hour Has Arrived or by using an Activate action to flip the tile and reveal The Power of The Black Cauldron.

There are no Activate actions in the Horned King's Realm. Ancient Soldiers add an Activate action to their location.

sections.title: Making Cauldron Born
sections.text:
You need Ancient Soldiers to make the Cauldron Born.

With The Power of The Black Cauldron revealed, you can now replace Ancient Soldiers with Cauldron Born. On your turn, before you move to a new location, you may pay 2 Power and discard an Ancient Soldier from your Realm to place a Cauldron Born from your hand into any location.

sections.title: Gurgi's Sacrifice and The Black Cauldron
sections.text: Gurgi's Sacrifice flips The Power of The Black Cauldron back to The Black Cauldron. While The Black Cauldron side is showing, the Horned King discards one Cauldron Born in play at the start of every turn BEFORE moving to a new location. You will need to use an Activate action to flip The Black Cauldron back to The Power of The Black Cauldron to make more Cauldron Born.

Gaston.objective: Gaston has many Obstacles to overcome in order to convince Belle he's the perfect man. By using his Allies and Effect cards, he can remove Obstacles and limit the impact of the Heroes who replace Obstacles in his Realm.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: Place one Obstacle Token on each of the eight indicated spots in Gaston’s Realm.

sections.title: Remove Obstacles with Effects
sections.text: Effect cards such as Temper, Come Into the Light, and Get Out allow Gaston to directly remove Obstacles. These cards cost plenty of Power, so replacing an Obstacle Token to gain Power when you play Swoon might help you out in the long run.

sections.title: Remove Obstacles with Allies
sections.text: Monsieur D’Arque will help remove Obstacle Tokens by using an Activate action and paying 2 Power.

sections.title: Remove Obstacles by Vanquishing Heroes
sections.text: Vanquishing Maurice and Beast allows Gaston to remove Obstacles from specific locations in his Realm. If there are no Obstacle Tokens in those locations, no Obstacles are removed.

sections.title: Replace Obstacles
sections.text:
Fate Effect cards such as I’ve Never Seen So Many Books, Saving My Life, It Is You, and Massaging My Feet replace Obstacle Tokens in Gaston’s Realm. The player who plays the Fate Effect card decides where to replace Obstacle Tokens. Only one Obstacle Token may be played to each spot.

While in play, Belle prevents Gaston from removing Obstacles.

Lady Tremaine.objective: To achieve Lady Tremaine's Objective, the Prince must be played from her Fate deck to The Ballroom, which must be unlocked by playing Invitation From the King, and you must move Ball Gown Drizella or Ball Gown Anastasia to The Ballroom. While there, you must activate the Wedding Bells card.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: The Ballroom starts the game locked: put a Lock Token on it. Lady Tremaine can't move there until it's unlocked.

sections.title: Going to the Ball
sections.text:
Once The Ballroom is unlocked by playing Invitation From the King, The Ballroom cannot be re-locked.

Only four characters can be played or moved to The Ballroom: The Prince (who is played there immediately when revealed), Ball Gown Cinderella, Ball Gown Drizella, and Ball Gown Anastasia.

While in play, Ball Gown Cinderella prevents Ball Gown Drizella or Ball Gown Anastasia from entering The Ballroom. This card has no effect if they are already there.

Sweet Nightingale is a powerful Fate card that may slow your progress to The Ballroom by moving any Ally to a new location.

Ball Gown Cinderella, Ball Gown Drizella, and Ball Gown Anastasia can only be played by first playing Cinderella, Drizella, or Anastasia in their everyday dresses then discarding them to play their Ball Gown versions to the same location. This swap requires a Play a Card action. There can never be two versions of a character in play at the same time.

Example: Swap Drizella for Ball Gown Drizella, who is played to the same location.

Important: Fairy Godmother can play Ball Gown Cinderella even if Cinderella is not in play. If this occurs, you may play Ball Gown Cinderella to any unlocked location.

sections.title: Trapped!
sections.text:
Cards like Lucifer, The Key, and Trapped allow you to place a Trapped Token on a Hero in your Realm. When a Hero has a Trapped Token, their Ability is ignored, as if the card has no Ability at all. The card still remains in play and blocks your actions. If a Trapped Hero is removed and placed in the Fate discard pile, remove the Trapped Token as well.

Ball Gown Cinderella cannot be Trapped by any card, although she can still be moved using the Activate action of The Key.

Lady Tremaine has no Vanquish actions. However, players can use Activate actions to discard or defeat Fate cards from play. Cards such as Lady Tremaine’s Cane, Midnight, and You Little Thief all remove specific Hero and Item cards from your Realm.

sections.title: Glass Slippers
sections.text:
Unlike other Items in the Fate card deck, Glass Slippers do not attach to a Hero. You cannot win the game while a Glass Slipper is in your Realm. You can remove a Glass Slipper by Activating Lady Tremaine's Cane.

Note: The Prince card is a Prince, not a Hero. The Prince is not affected by cards targeting Heroes.

Oogie Boogie.objective: Oogie Boogie wants to become the new ruler of Halloween Town. With Jack Skellington trying to take over Christmas, the path is clear for Oogie Boogie to dominate. But soon Jack will know that he truly is the Pumpkin King and will be back to take over. Oogie Boogie must prepare for the fight to come.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: Place the Sandy Claws card at Oogie Boogie's Lair face up. Set Oogie Boogie's dice off to the side near your Realm.

sections.title: How to Win
sections.text: Oogie Boogie knows the only way to become the ruler of Halloween Town is to defeat Jack Skellington, but Jack is the Impostor Sandy Claws. Oogie Boogie must play Impostor Sandy Claws cards from his Villain deck. The more Impostor Sandy Claws cards that are successfully played, the closer Jack is to remembering who he is and coming back to face Oogie Boogie.

sections.title: Impostor Jack
sections.text: When Oogie Boogie has successfully removed four Impostor Sandy Claws cards from his deck and placed them in a pile next to Sandy Claws, remove Sandy Claws from the game. Find Jack Skellington and place him in Oogie Boogie's Lair. Place the four Impostor Sandy Claws cards into Oogie Boogie's Villain discard pile.

sections.title: Rolling Dice
sections.text: Some of Oogie Boogie's cards allow him to roll his dice. Play the card as normal. Then, roll the dice. The results of the dice are included on the card. Oogie Boogie may not win every roll, but he rarely loses. Even bad rolls result in something that can work in Oogie Boogie's plan for defeating Jack.

sections.title: Dice Hijinx
sections.text:
Oogie Boogie cheats, especially when it comes to dice rolls. He even has cards that say so! After any dice rolls, Oogie Boogie may play Loaded Dice immediately (no Play a Card action needed). Loaded Dice allows Oogie Boogie to reroll one of the dice he just rolled.

To slow down the cheating Oogie Boogie, place the Fate card Hello, Oogie! under the Oogie Boogie mover. Hello, Oogie! reduces the next dice roll result by 2, after any rerolls. You may stack Hello, Oogie! cards and subtract that total. Discard Hello, Oogie! after rolling the dice.

sections.title: Changes to Strength
sections.text: Use +1/-1 Strength tokens to indicate changes to Hero and Ally Strength.

Sanderson Sisters.objective: The Sanderson Sisters, Winifred, Mary and Sarah, all want one thing: to live forever! To do this cursed action, they must brew the Life Potion and give it to either Max, Dani, or Allison, the heroes trying to stop them. By cursing Salem and brewing the potion, the Sanderson Sisters will be younger, more beautiful, live forever and be the evilest Villains ever!

sections.title: Setup
sections.text: Stack the Recipe cards in numerical order near your Realm. Flip the top card so the cards look like a book. Place the Witches' Cauldron tile, the Ingredient tokens, and the Life Potion token near your Realm.

sections.title: Sanderson Sisters
sections.text: In addition to the mover, each of the Sanderson Sisters has a Witch card. The Witches have an ability that gives them more strength the more Witches are in play. The Witches are considered Allies.

sections.title: Brewing the Life Potion
sections.text:
There are 6 pages to creating the Life Potion. You must complete the requirement on each card in order to brew the horrible elixir. When revealing cards, reveal them like a book.

Once the recipe for the ingredient is completed, take the corresponding token and place it in the Witches' Cauldron, then move on to the next recipe card to add the next ingredient. Only one ingredient can be added per turn.

• Witches' Cauldron: When a Witch is played to the Sanderson Sisters' Cottage, place the Witches' Cauldron tile near your Realm.

• Oil of Boil: When you spend 5 or more Power on your turn, place Oil of Boil token on the Witches' Cauldron tile.

• Dead Man's Toe: When you Vanquish a Hero, place Dead Man's Toe token on the Witches' Cauldron tile.

• Newt Saliva: When you have a Witch or Ally in three different locations, place Newt Saliva token on the Witches' Cauldron tile.

• Dash of Pox: When you have two or more Heroes at Dennisons' House, place Dash of Pox token on the Witches' Cauldron tile.

• Thine Own Tongue: When you perform three Activate actions on the same turn, place Thine Own Tongue token on the Witches' Cauldron tile.

sections.title: Using the Life Potion
sections.text:
When you have brewed the Life Potion, attach the token to a Hero in play. If there is no Hero in play, you must attach it to the next Hero played. If that Hero is somehow removed from play, attach it to next Hero that is played.

All three Witch cards (the Sisters themselves), the Life Potion, and the mover must be in the same location with a Hero. Vanquish the Hero to achieve your Objective.

Note: Binx cannot be defeated with the Life Potion.

sections.title: Hallowed Ground and Salt
sections.text: Hallowed Ground has different Fate Item rules. It is attached to a location and not a Hero. It blocks any actions in that location as a Hero does. You cannot take a Vanquish action at a location with Hallowed Ground. Salt works just like any normal Fate Item.

Prince Hans.objective: As the thirteenth-born son, Prince Hans will weave any story to become the prince of a Realm, and the Realm he is targeting is Arendelle. Using charm, lies, and the unfortunate, never-ending winter caused by Elsa, he pursues his ruthless plan to become the savior of Arendelle! To see his villainous plans come to fruition, he must defeat both Elsa and Anna to take their throne and the kingdom.

sections.title: Setup
sections.text:
Start the game with the Realm on the unfrozen side.

Place a Frozen Ring token over one action in each location. Place the rest near your board.

sections.title: The Freezing of Arendelle
sections.text:
Elsa has lost control of her powers and is freezing Arendelle in an endless winter.

Place Frozen Ring tokens over the various actions in the Realm. Hans can use any uncovered action, frozen or not. You can place Frozen Ring tokens on actions covered by Heroes. Cards like Monster! and Sorcery! help Hans place Frozen Ring tokens on his Realm.

Note: Prince Hans can play a Frozen Ring token to any location if he defeats a Hero in a Vanquish action.

sections.title: The Endless Winter
sections.text:
Once all sixteen actions on the Realm are covered with Frozen Ring tokens, remove all tokens, note the locations of Prince Hans, Allies and Heroes, then flip over the entire Realm. Place Prince Hans, Allies and Heroes back at the same locations in the Frozen Realm. Place Frozen Ring tokens over two actions in each location. This ends Prince Hans' turn.

Hans must again fill actions with Frozen Ring tokens. Once a frozen location has 4 Frozen Ring tokens on it, it is considered fully frozen.

sections.title: The Duke and His Guards
sections.text:
When Prince Hans moves to the Duke of Weselton's location, you may trigger the Duke's ability any time during that turn.

Francis' and Erik's abilities are always active and both can be triggered whenever an Effect is played.

sections.title: The Power of Elsa!
sections.text: Elsa has a very powerful ability. Prince Hans cannot perform an action at Elsa's location if it has a Frozen Ring token on it. Prince Hans can counter that restriction with I Love Crazy and So Desperate For Love to gain actions.

sections.title: The Sisters
sections.text:
Once any location is fully frozen, Prince Hans may Vanquish Elsa or Anna there. If either sister is Vanquished at a fully frozen location, they are not discarded. Instead, they are given to Prince Hans to set aside. That character is no longer in the game. Once Prince Hans has both sisters, he truly is the most Villainous of Kings!

Note: Anna and Elsa do not need to be defeated on the same turn or at the same fully frozen location to win the game.

Ernesto de la Cruz.objective: Ernesto de la Cruz is a beloved musician, actor, performer and hero to many... and above all that he is a backstabbing, song-stealing FRAUD! He maintains his lavish status in the Land of the Dead, but Ernesto's past is beginning to unravel thanks to Miguel Rivera, the rest of the Rivera family, and the one person who lived and died the truth, Héctor Rivera. As long as Ernesto can keep the secret and eliminate the main proof of his crimes (the photo and the memory of Héctor, the real creative genius), he can ensure the world will always remember the Great Hero Ernesto de la Cruz!

sections.title: Setup
sections.text: Place the photo cards near Ernesto's realm as shown. The top right card should be face down to start the game.

sections.title: The Photo
sections.text:
The one item that can drag down the powerful Ernesto de la Cruz is the photo of Héctor, Mamá Imelda and Coco Rivera, so it must be destroyed. The photo is destroyed when all six cards are face down.

Ernesto has multiple cards in his deck to help him flip sections of the photo. One of the most powerful is Forgetting Me. Choose a card and flip all adjacent cards. It may be two or three cards, depending on what card is chosen.

Seize Your Moment is a powerful card; it allows multiple photo cards to be flipped. Ernesto must discard at least one Ally before discarding any Heroes at that location (including Héctor Rivera).

sections.title: The Rivera Family
sections.text: Miguel is both helpful and harmful to Ernesto de la Cruz, depending on who is playing or moving the card. Flip a card when Miguel is played; he can reveal or hide photo cards. When Miguel is moved, he may reveal or hide photo cards based on his new location.

sections.title: Héctor Rivera
sections.text: Ernesto cannot win the game if Héctor is in play, even if all the photo cards are face down. Héctor's Strength is always equal to 1 plus the number of face-up photo cards. His Strength can and will change multiple times during Ernesto's turns. The card's Strength must be confirmed before any Vanquish action occurs.

Lotso.objective:
Lotso wants to keep new toys in the Caterpillar room.

You need access to all the Strength Modifier tokens.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: Place Buzz Lightyear at the top of Lotso's Realm in the Caterpillar Room with his Guardian side facing up.

sections.title: Reducing Heroes' Strength
sections.text:
Lotso has two ways to reduce Heroes' Strength: with Vanquish actions and with cards. To reduce a Hero's Strength, add Strength modifier tokens to the card. For example, to reduce a Hero's Strength to 0, put Strength tokens equal to the Hero's current total Strength on their card.

Important: Unlike the normal rules, if a Hero in Lotso's Realm is at 0 Strength, they cannot use their ability.

When Lotso Vanquishes a Hero, he does not discard them from his Realm. Instead, he reduces their Strength to 0 using Strength tokens. The Hero stays on Lotso's Realm where they are. Lotso still discards the Ally or Allies used in the Vanquish action.

Lotso can also reduce Strength with specific cards like Patrolling All Night Long and New Toys Don't Stand A Chance. The Bookworm allows Lotso to lose Power to reduce a Hero's Strength by the same amount. Where's Your Kid Now? allows Lotso to reduce the Strength of any Hero in his location to 0. While Woody's Hat is in Lotso's Realm, it reduces the Strength of all Heroes in Lotso's Realm except Woody.

sections.title: The Caterpillar Room
sections.text: Lotso has several ways to move Heroes to the Caterpillar Room and keep them there. Stretch and Welcome to Sunnyside move Heroes into the Caterpillar Room. These can be used at any time regardless of a Hero's Strength.

sections.title: Controlling Lotso's Fate
sections.text: Some Heroes are more difficult for Lotso to subdue. For example, Rex's Strength can only be reduced by cards or by a Vanquish action if he is the only Hero in a location. Hamm can only be Vanquished by two or more Allies.

sections.title: Buzz Lightyear
sections.text:
Depending on his settings, Buzz Lightyear can be either Lotso's Ally or a Guardian of Heroes.

Buzz Lightyear starts as a Guardian. He is not considered a Hero and cannot be targeted by Vanquish actions. Original Factory Settings flips Buzz Lightyear to Demo Mode Buzz Lightyear, Lotso's Ally. Flip over the tile and move Demo Mode Buzz Lightyear to the bottom of Lotso's Realm.

Demo Mode Buzz Lightyear cannot be discarded from Lotso's Realm. Cards targeting Allies, such as Jessie and Lotso Was Special, do not affect Demo Mode Buzz Lightyear. Spanish Mode can flip Buzz Lightyear back to his Guardian side. Flip over the tile and move it back to the top of Lotso's Realm.

Either Buzz Lightyear or Demo Mode Buzz Lightyear must be in the Caterpillar Room for Lotso to win.

Madam Mim.objective: Win the Wizard's Duel by defeating all of Merlin's Transformations with Mim's Transformations.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: Separate Merlin's Transformation deck from Madam Mim's Fate deck. Take the top card from Merlin's Transformation deck and place it face up at the Dueling Ground.

sections.title: Madam Mim's Transformations
sections.text:
Madam Mim does not have Allies. Instead, she has Transformations, the different animal forms she takes in the Wizard's Duel against Merlin. Merlin also has Transformations, each of which can be defeated by specific Mim Transformations. There are no Heroes in Madam Mim's Fate deck.

Mim's Transformations are counted as Allies for the sake of opponents' Condition cards. For example, Madam Mim's opponents should count the number of Mim Transformations on her Realm to determine how many "Allies" are in her Realm.

The Move an Item or Ally action allows you to move a Mim Transformation card.

sections.title: Merlin's Transformations
sections.text:
Merlin's Transformation deck only contains Merlin Transformations. There will always be at least one Merlin Transformation card in Madam Mim's Realm. Once a Merlin Transformation card is defeated, discard the card from your Realm into a separate discard pile just for Merlin Transformation cards. Then, immediately reveal and play a new Merlin Transformation card to the Dueling Ground. If there are no more cards in Merlin's Transformation deck and no Merlin Transformations in Madam Mim's Realm, Madam Mim wins the game.

Merlin's Transformations are counted as Heroes for the sake of opponents' Condition cards. For example, Madam Mim's opponents should count the number of Merlin Transformations on her Realm to determine how many "Heroes" are in her Realm. Also, if Madam Mim defeats a Merlin Transformation, this counts as defeating a Hero. The Move a Hero action allows you to move a Merlin Transformation card.

sections.title: Madam Mim's Fate Deck
sections.text:
Madam Mim has few Fate cards. When Madam Mim is the target of a Fate action, her opponent draws from this deck. Since there are so few cards, it may need to be reshuffled often.

Archimedes can interfere with Madam Mim's plans by replacing one Merlin Transformation with another. First, a Merlin Transformation is played to the same location as a Merlin Transformation (or Transformations) already in your Realm. Then, your opponent will choose one of the Merlin Transformations at that location and shuffle it back into Merlin's deck.

sections.title: A Wizard's Duel
sections.text:
Madam Mim has no Vanquish actions. Instead, each of her Transformations adds a Vanquish action to its location.

Each of Mim's Transformations can only defeat specific Merlin Transformations:

• Crocodile Mim Vanquishes Turtle Merlin

• Fox Mim Vanquishes Rabbit Merlin

• Chicken Mim Vanquishes Caterpillar Merlin

• Elephant Mim Vanquishes Walrus Merlin

• Tiger Mim Vanquishes Mouse Merlin

• Rattlesnake Mim Vanquishes Mouse Merlin

• Rhinoceros Mim Vanquishes Crab Merlin

• Purple Dragon Mim Vanquishes Goat Merlin

I'll Make the Rules allows Madam Mim to defeat any Merlin Transformation in play.

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: Place Omnidroid v.X8 at Nomanisan Island at the bottom of Syndrome's Realm. Set the Omnidroid v.X9 tile on top of the Omnidroid v.10 tile and place both to the right side of your Realm.

sections.title: Using Omnidroids
sections.text: Syndrome can use Omnidroids in a Vanquish action, along with any Allies. All Omnidroids can be moved using the Move an Item or Ally action while at the bottom of Syndrome's Realm. Syndrome cannot move Omnidroids at the top of his Realm.

sections.title: Defeating an Omnidroid
sections.text: Omnidroid v.X8 and Omnidroid v.X9 have a unique ability that triggers only after they have been defeated in a Vanquish action. Once Vanquished, use their Ability before removing the tile. That tile will no longer be used in this game. Omnidroid v.X8 must be defeated before Omnidroid v.X9 is played, and Omnidroid v.X9 must be defeated before Omnidroid v.10 can be played.

sections.title: Upgrading Omnidroids
sections.text:
Upgrade to Omnidroid v.X9 or v.10 by removing the correct number of Major Modifications from your Realm and placing the new Omnidroid tile in the location indicated. This is a free action with no Power Cost and can be done anytime during Syndrome's turn. Place removed cards into the discard pile.

Important: There can never be more than one Omnidroid card in Syndrome's Realm at any time.

sections.title: Syndrome's Remote
sections.text:
Syndrome cannot win the game unless Syndrome's Remote is in his Realm. When Syndrome is in Omnidroid v.10's location and Syndrome's Remote is at the bottom of his Realm, he must activate the Remote to defeat Omnidroid v.10.

When a Hero is played to Syndrome's Realm, attach Syndrome's Remote to them and immediately move Omnidroid v.10 to the bottom of Syndrome's Realm at the same location of the Hero with Syndrome's Remote.

Once a Hero with Syndrome's Remote has been defeated, Syndrome's Remote moves back to the bottom of Syndrome's Realm. Omnidroid v.10 then moves to the top of Syndrome's Realm.

Syndrome's Remote can be moved using the Move an Item or Ally action while on the bottom of Syndrome's Realm.

sections.title: Omnidroid v.10
sections.text:
Omnidroid v.10 is initially played to Downtown Metroville. If Syndrome's Remote is not in Syndrome's Realm, play Omnidroid v.10 to the top of Syndrome's Realm. Omnidroid v.10 is not discarded when used in a Vanquish action.

When Omnidroid v.10 has been defeated by using Syndrome's Remote, flip the tile over. Omnidroid v.10 can no longer be moved.

sections.title: Reducing Strength
sections.text: To reduce a Hero's Strength, add Strength tokens to the Hero card. For example, to reduce a Hero's Strength to 0, put Strength tokens equal to their current total Strength on their card.

Davy Jones.objective: The near-immortal Davy Jones, captain of the Flying Dutchman, is the judge over life and death on the seas. When he has control of all his mystic items, he not only controls the seas, but is worshiped and feared by all who sail those waters. Now Jack Sparrow has launched a series of events forcing Davy Jones to find and reclaim his treasures scattered among the Heroes. Davy Jones must find the Heroes and collect his treasures to take his rightful place as the ultimate ruler of all the seas!

sections.title: Lost Treasures Setup
sections.text: Place the five Treasure tokens face down off to the side of your realm, then mix them up. Davy Jones places a facedown Treasure token on Heroes when he plays the cards Do You Fear Death? and They're Here.

sections.title: Collecting Treasure
sections.text:
To collect a Treasure, Davy Jones must first reveal it and then defeat the Hero that Treasure is attached to. Certain cards, such as Bootstrap Bill, Hadras, and The Black Spot, reveal facedown tokens.

If Davy Jones defeats a Hero with a facedown Treasure token, that token is returned to the starting supply of tokens.

Note: A Hero may only have one Treasure token attached to them at a time.

sections.title: The Power of the Treasures
sections.text:
Each Treasure token has a unique ability. When the token is revealed, that ability will affect the Hero or make it harder for Davy Jones to retrieve his property. The Treasure tokens take effect immediately when they are revealed.

• The Key: When The Key is revealed docard your hand.

• The Heart: When The Heart is collected lose all Power.

• Treasure Chest: Allies cannot be played to this location.

• Music Box: The Kraken cannot be used to defeat this Hero.

• Jack's Compass: This Hero gets +2 Strength.

sections.title: Those Pesky Heroes
sections.text: Heroes can make it difficult for Davy Jones to find his treasures. Where Does It Point? and Curse You, Jack Sparrow keep Davy Jones guessing on where the Heroes might be and what Treasure they may hold.

Tamatoa.objective: Not only is Tamatoa the cleverest monster in the sea, he is also the shiniest. His power and ego are limitless as he hoards what everyone wants, including the demigod Maui's Hook. He needs to keep Maui from reclaiming his Hook and try to grab the Heart of Te Fiti from Moana. If he can overcome these Heroes and their plans, he can become the crustacean with the power of creation and the most feared monster ever!

sections.title: Special Setup
sections.text: Tamatoa uses a third deck called the Maui deck. Place the deck close to your Villain deck.

sections.title: The Maui Deck
sections.text: The Maui deck is a mysterious bag of effects. Tamatoa draws a Maui card while Maui is in play and before Tamatoa moves to a new location. The effects of the Maui card are immediate and may change what happens during that turn. Tamatoa also may play Not Exactly Maui Time to reveal a card and either play or discard it.

sections.title: Maui's Hook
sections.text: Maui's Hook can be found in Tamatoa's Villain deck. Tamatoa can play it as an Item card that is not attached to an Ally. While Maui's Hook is on Tamatoa's side of the Realm, Tamatoa gains 2 Power cach time he is Fated. The Fate card Maui Time finds Maui and automatically finds and attaches Maui's Hook to him. If Maui is defeated while Maui's Hook is attached to him, move Maui's Hook to Tamatoa's side of the Realm at that location.

sections.title: Heart of Te Fiti
sections.text: When the Fate card Heart of Te Fit is drawn, it finds Moana and is attached to her. Tamatoa needs to defeat Moana while the Heart of Te Fiti is attached to her to gain the Item and win the game. Heart of Te Fiti can be moved using a Move Ally or Item action when it is on Tamatoa's side of the Realm.

sections.title: ...But it's a Fake!
sections.text: Something Shiny is the ultimate trick Moana plays on Tamatoa. The Item is not attached to a Hero but is played like a Hero to cover actions. A Hero at the same location as Something Shiny cannot be defeated. Something Shiny is discarded when Tamatoa ends his turn in the same location as Something Shiny.

sections.title: Heihei
sections.text: The Fate card Heihei has no additional ability.

Shere Khan.objective: Fierce Shere Khan controls the jungle, but he has a weakness: Man's Red Fire! When he discovers a Man-Cub in his jungle, he must stop the boy before he destroys everything. Mowgli wants to stay in the jungle and is protected by his friends, including Baloo the bear, the elephants of the Jungle Patrol, and even the great panther Bagheera. Shere Khan must clear his realm of fire and defeat Mowgli to prove he is still King of the Jungle.

sections.title: Setup
sections.text: Place the four Fire Tokens off to the side of your Realm.

sections.title: Kaa, His Eyes and His Coils
sections.text: Shere Khan's Ally, Kaa, has muttiple ways to help Shere Khan. You can attach Kaas Eyes and Kare Coils to Kaa as Items to increase his Strength to 4 or even 6! When used in a Vanquish action, you can remove those Items instead of Kaa. You can use Kaa's Activate action to find those Items in the discard pile.

sections.title: Man's Red Fire
sections.text:
Fire tokens are placed using the Fate cards Mowgli and Man's Red Fire. A Fire token can be placed on a single action, which is treated as if covered by a Hero card. The Fire token can be placed on any action in the top or bottom row of Shere Khan's Realm. If a card is played to or already exists at that location, the token can still be placed on an action, but both will need to be removed before that action can be taken.

Bravo! Bravo! will let you perform a blocked action, even if it's covered by a Fire token.

sections.title: Manipulating Cards
sections.text: Hey Cuz and Trust In Me allow you to manipulate the cards in your Villain deck and discard pile. Hey Cuz lets you reveal cards until you find an Ally. Trust in Me lets you shuffle three cards from your discard pile into your deck.

sections.title: Removing Fire Tokens
sections.text: To remove Fire tokens, use the Activate action on Monkeys. It's Me, Shere Khan removes a token without sacrificing an Ally.

sections.title: Fight Like a Bear
sections.text: Baloo has a unique power that affects defeating and vanquishing all other Heroes. While Baloo is in play, if Shere Khan defeats a Hero, that Hero is not removed. Instead, place a Power token on Baloo. When Baloo has three Power tokens on him, he is defeated. Baloo can protect Heroes this way before he is defeated and discarded.

King Candy.objective: King Candy is the ultimate ruler of Sugar Rush, but one thing stands in the way of him controlling the game and his world forever: Vanellope von Schweetz. He needs to attach a Glitch to Vanellope von Schweetz, then beat her in a Sugar Rush race. Wreck-It Ralph and her other new friends will try to slow him down, but King Candy has his own tricks; not just to win the race, but to be King forever!

sections.title: Special Setup and Movement
sections.text:
Place King Candy's mover on the Start/Finish. Set the Vanellope von Schweetz Racer token off to the side of your Realm. King Candy moves like no other Villain; he races through the entire Sugar Rush Speedway, moving from action space to action space in the figure-8 pattern shown below. He passes the center Gain 3 Power twice on a single circuit.

Each tum before King Candy moves, declare the number of action spaces you want to move, between 1 and 4. An action space counts for movement even if covered.

sections.title: Special Free Actions
sections.text: King Candy has access to cards that he can play without a Play a Card action. Pay to Race is paid and played before King Candy declares his movement. Turbo-Tastic allows King Candy to perform actions that are currently covered.

sections.title: Performing Actions
sections.text:
Once King Candy has moved, he may perform the action he is on, the action in front of him on the track and the action behind him, for a total of three actions on his tum. They can be performed in any order. If an action is covered. King Candy cannot perform that action. King Candy may end up with no available actions.

Start/Finish is a Play a Card action.

Even though King Candy's Realm is one continuous speedway, each panel represents a location that is used in Vanquish actions.

sections.title: The Big Race
sections.text:
When a Glitch is played on Vanellope von Schweetz, begin the Big Race by placing the Racer token and the King Candy mover on Start/Finish. End King Candy's turn. Note that multiple Glitches can be stacked on Vanellope von Schweetz, but the Big Race only begins if a Glitch is placed on her when she has no other Glitches attached.

If King Candy reaches Start/Finish before the Racer token, he wins the game. If the Racer token reaches Start/Finish first, remove all the Glitches from Vanellope von Schweetz and place them in King Candy's hand.
